newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends day softer, confused by gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends day softer, confused by gasoline.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended a day of mediocre volume trading, softer in line with Brent crude oil and on indications that Iraq was making progress towards its second round of "oil-for-food" deal. Brokers said choppy trading on the NYMEX unleaded gasoline left gas oil traders at a bit of a loss on market direction.
The prompt August gas oil contract closed 50 cents down at $167 a tonne. The August/September spread settled at -$1.50, having traded in a narrow range for most of the day.

"The gasoline is all over the shop and that makes gas oil traders worried. With the low volume trade on gas oil for most of the day there hasn't been an opportunity for people to take positions," a broker said adding that the next support level on gas oil was at $166.25-166 a tonne.

NYMEX traders said August gasoline futures were being squeezed, prior to expiry on Thursday, as key to the strength seen on the contract on Monday. The contract had started the day stronger and reached a high at 65.05 cents, but soon slid sharply lower, trailing the weakness in the crude prices. It last traded up 0.72 cents at 64.75 cents a gallon.
September Brent crude oil traded seven cents up at $18.54 a barrel at 1711 GMT.
Eyes remained focused on Iraq and any further developments on their upcoming crude oil sales.
"The market is nervous about Iraq and what it is going to do," one London based broker said.

Nizar Hamdoon, Iraq's ambassador to the U.N. said on Monday that Iraq had delivered annexes to its aid distribution plan to the U.N. today. This would allow the U.N. to review and accept the document in the next few days.
He also said Iraq still hoped the U.N. would change its mind and allow Baghdad to make up time lost since June 8 by putting back the start.
